title: LLMs for Builders
subtitle: APIs, Tokens, and the Developer Model
footer_text: LLMs for Builders — APIs, Tokens, and the Developer Model
context: Working backend developers who use LangChain but have never called an LLM API directly. They can read Python and know what an HTTP request is. The module strips the framework away and works at the raw API layer, so they can debug and extend rather than only follow tutorials.

blocks.brief: What the reader will be able to do after this module: raw sync and async calls to OpenAI and Anthropic; tokens and counting them with tiktoken as the cost and capacity unit; a cost estimator that predicts a chain's cost before running it; structured output and function calling for validated JSON; a retry wrapper with exponential backoff that later modules reuse; prompt injection and defending against it at the API layer.

LangChain and LangGraph are good abstractions, but when something breaks you need to know what is underneath. This module works directly against the HTTP APIs so that by Module 02 the reader knows what LangChain is doing for them and when to step around it.

Describe the module project: a Structured Document Extractor. Takes unstructured text such as an invoice, email or article; defines the output shape with a Pydantic schema; calls the OpenAI API in structured output mode; returns validated JSON; prints token usage and estimated cost per run. Around 80 lines, annotated, copy-paste ready. Open with the project name in bold.

Every LangChain tutorial opens with an import and that is fine for getting moving, but it hides that every LLM call is ultimately an HTTP POST to an endpoint. Knowing that endpoint — request structure, response format, error codes — separates a developer who can only follow tutorials from one who can debug and extend. Mention the import `from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI` as an inline code chip.

This series teaches the stack from the inside out: raw API layer first, then LangChain's abstractions in Module 02, agents in Module 04, multi-agent graphs in Module 06. By the time the reader builds production systems, every component makes sense because they built it from scratch.

blocks.caption: The LangChain abstraction stack. This module covers layers 0 and 1.

blocks.label: CONCEPT
blocks.brief: An LLM API is a stateless HTTP endpoint: every call is independent, with no memory and no continuity. When LangChain adds memory it is rebuilding conversation history in the prompt on every call. When an agent reasons over several steps it is making several separate API calls. Seeing this makes the whole agentic stack easier to reason about.

Two APIs dominate for builders: OpenAI's Chat Completions and Anthropic's Messages. Slightly different request structures and philosophies, same fundamental model — send a list of messages, get a completion back.
Name the OpenAI Chat Completions API as the subject of what follows.

The OpenAI Python SDK wraps the chat completions endpoint. The message list has three roles: system for instructions, user for input, assistant for prior model responses in multi-turn conversations. Use inline code chips for `openai==1.x` and `POST /v1/chat/completions`, and bold for the three role names.

A minimal but complete first call. Read the key from the environment, never hardcode it. Create the client, call chat.completions.create with a small model, a system message and a user message, a low temperature and a max_tokens cap. Then show how to pull the text out of the response and how to read prompt, completion and total tokens from usage. Comment the non-obvious lines.

blocks.label: CODE NOTE
blocks.subtitle: TEMPERATURE
blocks.brief: Explain that a low temperature is a sensible default for extraction and classification: near zero is close to deterministic, above one gets erratic. Make the point that it is not a quality dial.
